names.note: Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's second heading for the Julian 7 March on pravoslavno.rs, „Преподобни Емилијан.“, with the rank word Преподобни left off. The heading gives no epithet and no place; Rome is in the body's first sentence, and the English epithet this folder carries is a chosen one and not a form of any name the source prints. `Емилијан` is held by no other folder.

Read out of the title on the name link behind the line for 7 марта ст. ст., name page 776, «Емилиан Италийский, прп.», with the grade word left off; the day's own line declines it. The by-name is kept because the bare forename is already the fold this folder sits in — «емилијан», with `emilian-of-durostorum`, which the gate has read — and because the corpus holds nine other Emilians, one of them a martyr of Rome on this very day. `.tmp/foldchk.py` reports no folder holding this form and `.tmp/sr-foldpred.mjs` reports 0 other holders of the key it folds to, so neither the read fold nor any other is widened.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 7 марта ст. ст. — «Прп. Емилиана Италийского (VI).»

attestations.note: **The only one of the four calendars read that puts a life behind his name**, and the only one that gives him a century. The folder was made off the Охридски пролог, which prints the bare «Емилијан» under a rank word; this line adds the by-name Италийский, the name he was born with, the whole story of the cave and the voice, and the (VI) which is the first date this folder has ever carried. **The by-name is also what separates him from the other Emilian of this same day**: saint.gr keeps a martyr of Rome of about 259 on 7 March and this corpus holds him and his two companions as `emilian-the-roman`, `james-companion-of-emilian` and `marianus-companion-of-emilian`. Both men are Romans of one name; one is a martyr of the third century and this one a penitent of the sixth who died in his bed, and no relation is asserted between them.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for 7 martie, which is the page for this menologion number — not 20 martie, which merely shares his civil date in 2026.

Not checked: saint.gr's εορτολόγιο for 7 Μαρτίου, which is the page for this menologion number. That Greek day does carry an Emilian of Rome — «Άγιοι Αιμιλιανός ο Ρωμαίος και οι συν αυτώ Ιάκωβος και Μαριανός», which is the corpus's `emilian-the-roman` — but he is a martyr of 259 with two companions, and this man is a monk who reposed in the Lord after a long life; nothing was read that would make them one, and the two stories cannot both be one man's.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 20.03.2026 (7. март ст. ст.) — „Преподобни Емилијан.“

attestations.note: The day's second and last entry, and a new folder rather than an upgrade. The corpus's `emilian-the-roman` is kept by the Greek on this same menologion day and is also born at Rome, but he is a martyr who died in 259 with the companions James and Marianus, where this entry's man takes the monastic habit, is an example to his brethren, and lives long and reposes in the Lord — the heading calls him Преподобни and nothing in the entry is a martyrdom. Death by the sword against a peaceful repose is the kind of incompatibility this corpus reads as two men, as `kalia-12-february` was read against `kale`. The English name is a chosen form, because the only thing in the entry that distinguishes him from the other Emilian of Rome is his repentance; that choice is in the reader's report. No `dates`: the entry gives neither a year nor a century.

death.note: **The first date this folder has carried.** days.pravoslavie.ru closes its line for 7 марта ст. ст. with (VI) and its life gives neither a year, a reign nor a century of its own; the Охридски пролог behind the existing Serbian row gives nothing at all. The life has him die peacefully in his monastery after a late repentance, so the century is a century and no narrower bound is available from any page read.
